note: IFHA jointly presents Group/Graded quality-race categories; Group race and Grade race are corresponding system labels, not globally interchangeable headwords.
IFHA explicitly pairs Group 1 with Grade 1 as G1 quality-race descriptions across authorities.
IFHA explicitly pairs Group 2 with Grade 2 as G2 quality-race descriptions across authorities.
IFHA explicitly pairs Group 3 with Grade 3 as G3 quality-race descriptions across authorities.
Going and Track condition both describe racing-surface state but participate in different jurisdiction taxonomies; do not merge or assert exact equivalence.
Racecourse and Racetrack can refer to the overall racing venue, but Racetrack also has a physical-track sense. Exact equivalence is therefore unsafe globally.
Track can colloquially denote a racecourse/venue, but also denotes the racing surface/path. Preserve polysemy rather than merge.
Track and Course overlap when referring to the physical route or running surface but neither is globally identical across all racing contexts.
A Fixture is an officially scheduled racing unit in the BHA fixture list; a Race meeting is the racing event/collection of races. Scheduling relation does not prove identity.
Race day describes the day or day's racing; Race meeting describes the event/collection. They often coincide but are not universally the same Concept.

scope: AUS/NZ rest-period terminology vs general layoff
note: NZ usage defines Spelling as a recuperative break; Layoff is a broader absence from racing. Related but not asserted exact-equivalent.
Favorite and Longshot occupy contrasting market-support/price positions; this is a contrast relation, not a strict logical antonym claim.
France Galop Meeting is a series of Réunions; MEET-001 represents the one-day Réunion sense. They are structurally related but not synonyms.
Réunion Premium is a France-specific subtype/classification of a one-day Réunion/Race meeting.
Réunion PMH is a France-specific subtype/classification of a one-day Réunion/Race meeting.

scope: Tactical pacemaker role vs generic pacesetter
note: A tactical pacemaker intentionally makes the pace to benefit another aligned runner; every tactical pacemaker is pace-making, but a generic Pacesetter need not have that purpose.
